queue.note: Ready, parked and blocked are reported together: a queue showing only ready work looks identical whether twelve requirements are parked on a credential or none are.

reconciliation.note: Executable means this build owes it; ready means nothing is stopping it now. A half-built requirement whose remainder waits on a credential is both owed and parked, which is why these are two numbers rather than one.

benchmark_observation.what: read-only Etsy API credentials that can actually serve a request
benchmark_observation.how_it_is_checked: a recorded etsy.probe succeeded -- a real sanctioned read, not a variable being set

model_provider.what: a model provider that can actually serve a request
model_provider.how_it_is_checked: a recorded model.probe succeeded -- a real call, not a variable being set

etsy_shop.what: a live Etsy shop, which only the account holder can open
etsy_shop.how_it_is_checked: the shop's public identifier is set AND a recorded etsy.probe succeeded -- the identifier alone is a variable, which is not a shop

etsy_api.what: Etsy API credentials, which are what lets this system read the shop's own seller data rather than a person reading it on a screen
etsy_api.how_it_is_checked: a recorded etsy.probe succeeded -- a real sanctioned read, not a variable being set

image_vision.what: a model that can actually look at a picture, over the gallery URLs the sanctioned Etsy endpoint already returns
image_vision.how_it_is_checked: a recorded vision.probe judged a real observed image -- and a reply that describes no image is recorded as a failure, because a 200 carrying an apology is the shape a broken vision path takes

rendered_pages.what: a browser worker that can fetch an Etsy page as a buyer sees it: Marketplace Insights, search results and policy pages have no endpoint among the nine this application is authorised for
rendered_pages.how_it_is_checked: a recorded browser.probe fetched a real rendered page -- a configured worker URL is a string, and Etsy answers 403 to a great many of them -- OR every etsy.com/legal policy source has a page reading by a named person, recorded through POST /api/policy/snapshot within 30 days, with no unreviewed material change (platform_policy.page_readings_status)

transactions_r.what: the owner has re-authorised the Etsy app with the transactions_r scope, so receipts can be read (C-64: the order source)
transactions_r.how_it_is_checked: the stored Etsy grant lists transactions_r AND a successful etsy.probe is recorded; the scope is added only by the owner in a browser (owner action reauthorise_transactions_r), and the ingest makes no network call while closed

insights_access.how_it_is_checked: at least one InsightsSnapshot row exists -- a reading somebody recorded from Shop Manager, counted, because there is no sanctioned endpoint that returns it

acceptance_ruling.what: the owner has ruled whether an API+vision traversal satisfies the browser/vision wording of #189/#221/#222/#320
acceptance_ruling.how_it_is_checked: an OwnerAction with requirement_key 'decision.api_vision_equivalence' is done -- a decision only the owner can make, recorded rather than assumed

tester_roster.what: one person who has agreed to test a Brambleloop pattern, which needs outreach to real people and therefore an exit from shadow mode
tester_roster.how_it_is_checked: at least one CreatorProfile has agreed -- delivered > 0 or a recorded permission. A prospect on file is not a tester

image_generation.what: an image-generation provider that conditions on reference images, because an identity lock is reference conditioning rather than a better prompt
image_generation.how_it_is_checked: a recorded image.probe generated a real image -- and a provider that refuses this brief on content grounds is a refusal in its own words, never an empty gallery

canonical_model.what: the owner's approval of a canonical model identity, which is a decision rather than a capability -- no amount of rendering produces it
canonical_model.how_it_is_checked: a ModelIdentity row is canonical with an owner approval timestamp. `select` refuses to promote a candidate without one, so a better picture cannot make this true

benchmark_purchases.what: the approved 13-pattern MJs benchmark set (CA$300 ceiling), bought by the owner and uploaded at /ops/teardown
benchmark_purchases.how_it_is_checked: at least one BenchmarkProduct row exists -- counted, not asked about

production_window.what: the owner's authorisation to run this build in production for a full unattended window, so the off-device proof can be read from real rows
production_window.how_it_is_checked: autonomy.launch_item reads PROVEN from the rows a full production window left

offsite_storage.what: an object-storage bucket and credential outside this provider, so a copy of the continuity archive survives losing the provider itself
offsite_storage.how_it_is_checked: a continuity archive has actually been written offsite. A typed bucket address that is wrong, or whose credentials are, survives losing this provider exactly as well as no bucket at all

owned_surfaces.what: an owned publishing surface beyond the Etsy shop (which exists and is the paid destination): a site and/or Pinterest account, opened by the owner
owned_surfaces.how_it_is_checked: the latest owned_surface.probe audit row records ok: true -- a real publish-path check, not a site URL or token variable being set

live_listings.what: a listing that exists on the marketplace: company work first (a product clears the final publication gate), then the owner's per-listing publication grant
live_listings.how_it_is_checked: at least one Listing row carries an Etsy listing id -- counted, not read from the phase flag, because a phase is a statement of intent and a listing id is a listing

customers.what: real orders, which only a buyer can create -- DATA/EXTERNAL-gated, never an owner action (closure.DATA_GATES; listed under waiting_on_data, never as an owner card)
customers.how_it_is_checked: at least one LedgerEntry has gross_cad > 0 and an evidence_ref -- revenue with its order, not an expense and not a phase flag saying the company is selling

physical_proof.what: a completed physical test of a Brambleloop pattern by whoever the testing protocol says performs one
physical_proof.how_it_is_checked: at least one PhysicalTest row has a completion date -- the intake being built is not the same as a finished object existing, and nothing here says whose hands finished it

second_market_benchmark.what: a benchmark shop outside the United States, which is a choice of shop rather than a credential or a capability
second_market_benchmark.how_it_is_checked: observed listings exist for two or more distinct stated markets -- one shop's term frequencies are one market's language however many listings they came from

culture_feed.what: a connected source of cultural signal -- search interest, social or trend data -- which this company has never had
culture_feed.how_it_is_checked: at least one CultureObservation row names the source it came from. An observation with no source is the same unverifiable thing as no observation

model_bearing_render.what: a model-bearing listing frame that clears every floor -- identity, morphology, product truth, photographic realism, asset truth and styling -- which no image provider has yet rendered
model_bearing_render.how_it_is_checked: an assets.model_photography audit row that is made, carries the model, is usable as a listing asset and reads `pass` on all six model_photography.FLOORS. `unverifiable` is not a pass, and a product-first frame does not count

ad_authority.what: an approved advertising budget -- recommended only once a listing is ready to sell (gate_clearance.ad_readiness)
ad_authority.how_it_is_checked: a SpendLimit row for 'ads' exists with a positive, unpaused daily cap

final_master.rule: ready iff zero launch-critical rows OPEN and no integrity violation; post-launch rows never block (F-400/F-879); only an explicit owner/data/external gate with a key removes work from OPEN (F-838)

note: The graph, the queue and the parking state live in Postgres, so losing a session loses a worker rather than the build. An owner action parks the requirements that need it and never holds the queue.

batches.rule: one decision per thing the owner answers: gates and producer rows that are the same decision are merged; related decisions are batched; an unknown cost is UNKNOWN, never CA$0

empty_state.rule: an empty queue closes nothing; the readiness closer still requires a non-empty assessment before closing (runtime.release 'if requests:')

approval_inbox.source: one queue: executor gate state merged with OwnerAction rows by requirement_key (build2.executor.approval_inbox)
approval_inbox.note: An inbox is only asynchronous if the queue behind it does not wait. 0 requirements are ready right now and none of them needs any of these answers; answering them un-parks 94 more (#196).

jobs_completed.why: work finished, not work enqueued -- a queue that only grows is a stall

distinct_job_types.why: more than one kind of work, or one retrying job counts as a company

activity_spread.why: completions spread across the window rather than clustered at the start, which is what a container that died after booting looks like

scheduler_alive.why: the scheduler enqueued cadence work in this many distinct hours -- counted from `cadence:` idempotency keys, which only `Scheduler.tick` writes, so hand-enqueued work and the system's own audit chatter cannot stand in for a scheduler that stopped

no_unexpected_dead_letters.why: a window full of dead letters is uptime, not work. Shadow-mode publish refusals are excluded from the count as well as from the test, so this number means what it says

restart_recovery.why: jobs that completed on a second or later attempt: retried after a failure or reclaimed after their worker stopped renewing its lease. Zero is a window with no restart to recover from, not a failure

off_device_proof.note: 'Online' means useful work is progressing, not that HTTP returns 200 (#185). A container answering health checks with a stalled queue passes every naive uptime monitor ever written, and it is the failure a hosted service produces most often -- the process is fine, the work stopped.

health.note: A queue with work in it and nothing completing is the failure that looks like uptime. Depth alone is not the signal; depth with no completions is.
